population.definition: Gaborone City (city proper, as tabulated in the 2022 Population and Housing Census, census date 18 March 2022). Read via citypopulation.de, which credits Statistics Botswana; the Statistics Botswana PDF itself could not be reached.

source.title: Botswana: Cities (census table)

facts.claim: Gaborone was laid out on almost empty ground from 1964 so that Botswana could be governed from inside its own borders (the protectorate had been run from Mafeking).

source.title: Gaborone, Capital of Botswana: The City Built From Scratch in Three Years
source.quote: Gaborone was laid out on almost empty ground from 1964 so Botswana could be governed from inside its own borders.

facts.claim: The administration of the Bechuanaland Protectorate moved from Mafeking to Gaberones in 1965, before independence in 1966.

source.title: Gaborone, Capital of Botswana: The City Built From Scratch in Three Years
source.quote: In 1965 the administration of the protectorate finally moved from Mafeking to Gaberones

facts.claim: The city is named after Kgosi Gaborone, a Batlokwa leader; the name is glossed as 'it does not fit badly'.

source.title: Gaborone
source.quote: Gaborone literally means 'it does not fit badly' or 'it is not unbecoming'.

facts.claim: Settlers turned 'Gaborone's village' into 'Gaberones'; the colonial spelling was dropped in 1969.

source.title: Gaborone, Capital of Botswana: The City Built From Scratch in Three Years
source.quote: in 1969 the city dropped the colonial spelling and became Gaborone.

facts.claim: The early town was planned on garden-city principles; its layout was compared to a brandy glass by the chairman of the Gaberones Township Authority, and most of it went up in about three years.

source.title: Gaborone, Capital of Botswana: The City Built From Scratch in Three Years
source.quote: Geoffrey Cornish, chairman of the Gaberones Township Authority, compared the plan to a brandy glass.

timeline.claim: Work on the new town started in mid-1964, following garden-city principles.

source.title: Gaborone, Capital of Botswana: The City Built From Scratch in Three Years
source.quote: Work on the town started in mid-1964 and followed garden city principles

timeline.claim: Protectorate administration moved from Mafeking to Gaberones.

source.title: Gaborone, Capital of Botswana: The City Built From Scratch in Three Years
source.quote: In 1965 the administration of the protectorate finally moved from Mafeking to Gaberones

timeline.claim: Gaborone became the capital as Botswana gained independence.

source.title: Gaborone History: How Botswana's Capital Took Shape
source.author: Joel Kaben
source.quote: Gaborone became the capital in 1966, the same year Botswana gained independence.

timeline.claim: The National Museum was established in Gaborone.

source.title: 50 years of Botswana's visual arts
source.author: Spira Tlhankane
source.quote: The National Museum was established in Gaborone in 1967

timeline.claim: The city dropped the colonial spelling Gaberones and became Gaborone.

source.title: Gaborone, Capital of Botswana: The City Built From Scratch in Three Years
source.quote: in 1969 the city dropped the colonial spelling and became Gaborone.

timeline.claim: Formal inauguration of the University of Botswana (its roots go back to the University of Basutoland, Bechuanaland and Swaziland, opened 1964).

source.title: History of UB
source.quote: formal inauguration of the University of Botswana was performed on October 23, 1982

timeline.claim: The Three Dikgosi Monument was inaugurated by President Festus Mogae.

source.title: The Three Dikgosi Monument - Commonwealth Walkway
source.quote: The monument was inaugurated on 29 September 2005 by Festus Mogae, President of Botswana at the time.

places.name: Three Dikgosi Monument
places.what: A bronze sculpture in the Gaborone central business district showing three Batswana chiefs who travelled to Britain in 1895. It was inaugurated in 2005.

facts.label: Who it depicts
facts.value: Khama III, Sebele I and Bathoen I

source.title: The Three Dikgosi Monument - Commonwealth Walkway
source.quote: Khama III of the Bangwato, Sebele I of the Bakwena, and Bathoen I of the Bangwaketse.

source.title: The Three Dikgosi Monument - Commonwealth Walkway
source.quote: The monument was inaugurated on 29 September 2005 by Festus Mogae, President of Botswana at the time.

source.title: The Three Dikgosi Monument - Commonwealth Walkway
source.quote: a bronze sculpture in the Gaborone CBD.

facts.label: Significance
facts.value: Marks a turning point in Botswana's history (tourism board)

source.title: Gaborone
source.quote: marks a significant turning point in Botswana's history.

places.name: Botswana National Museum and Art Gallery
places.what: The national museum in central Gaborone, with collections of traditional crafts and southern African fine art. It also includes the National Art Gallery, the Octagon Gallery and, since 2007, the National Botanical Garden.

source.title: Botswana National Museum
source.quote: Established in 1967 through an Act of Parliament, the museum opened its doors to the public in 1968.

source.title: Botswana National Museum and Art Gallery (Know Your Museums)
source.quote: Established in 1967

source.title: Botswana National Museum and Art Gallery (Know Your Museums)
source.quote: An art gallery and auditorium were added in 1973 (summarised by fetch tool; not verbatim)

source.quote: housing essential collections of traditional crafts and southern African fine art.

places.name: Gaborone Game Reserve
places.what: A small fenced reserve on the eastern edge of the city, near the Gaborone Dam. It is described as one of few national reserves inside a city.

source.title: Gaborone Game Reserve - Guide to Botswana's Urban Park
source.quote: 5-square-kilometre (600-hectare) enclave

facts.label: Managed by
facts.value: Department of Wildlife and National Parks (per this site)

places.name: Thapong Visual Arts Centre
places.what: An artists' centre in an old building in Gaborone Village, with studios for local artists. It grew out of the Thapong International Artists' Workshop founded in 1989.

source.title: 50 years of Botswana's visual arts
source.author: Mompati Tlhankane

places.name: University of Botswana
places.what: The national university, with its main campus in Gaborone. It was formally inaugurated in 1982 and grew out of a regional university founded in 1964.

source.title: History of UB
source.quote: formal inauguration of the University of Botswana was performed on October 23, 1982

facts.label: Predecessor
facts.value: University of Basutoland, Bechuanaland and Swaziland (1964)

source.title: History of UB
